mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4.5% relative to its 12-month moving average compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns through reduced cost of capital for corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for FEDFUNDS level against 20-day SPX returns remains below 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window, or correlation between FEDFUNDS level and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month, or average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in housing starts (HOUST) and real sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% indicate robust consumer demand and business investment, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns through elevated corporate earnings growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS (both >0.5% increase) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in > 40% of instances, or average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% signals an imminent economic slowdown that reduces corporate profit growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, INDPRO decline > 0.5% fails to produce negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances, or average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in CPIAUCSL exceeding 0.5 percentage points accelerates inflation expectations, triggering monetary policy tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in 1 month, or average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% monthly growth indicates strong labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Rank IC for PAYEMS growth against 20-day SPX returns falls below 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window, or correlation between PAYEMS growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansion regimes, a quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) exceeding 0.5% relative to the prior quarter signals robust economic momentum that elevates corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In early-cycle expansion periods, GDPC1 growth > 0.5% fails to produce positive 20-day returns in > 40% of instances, or average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% and CPIAUCSL rises below 0.2% indicate balanced economic growth without inflationary pressure, expanding corporate margins and generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL rises < 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint signal of INDPRO >0.5% increase and CPIAUCSL <0.2% increase fails to produce positive 20-day returns in > 40% of instances, or average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
